newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares recovered most of early losses at the end of Tuesday trading on relief over the lower than expected increase in Q4 U.S. job costs.
Option-related buying added to the rise, dealers said.
"With the Dow surging some 100 points in the first hour of trade, many players had to cover their option positions and bought baskets (of shares)," one dealer said.
He added the 'general public', seeing the upturn in the market, jumped on board and pushed prices further up.
Volume, which had been below average until the U.S. data, returned to normal levels after heavy afternoon trade.
Dealers said the number of basket trades showed the market was nervous. "They want to cover their options trade as soon as possible," one dealer said.
The AEX index of blue chips ended 0.70 points higher at 683.13, a strong recovery from its 674.84 midsession low.
Chemicals group DSM ended 4.30 guilders lower at 176.30 as the market digested a lower than expected 1996 preliminary net profits released before opening.
DSM said its 1996 ordinary net profit would be at least 700 milion guilders, 50 million guilders below analysts' consensus and a sharp decline compared with 1995's 1.073 billion guilders.
Sector companion Akzo followed DSM down but partly recovered to close at 264.60 guilders, 1.60 lower than Monday.
Unilever closed 3.80 guilders higher at 308.90 guilders, benefitting from the strong dollar, as did Royal Dutch which gained 3.10 to close at 320.10 guilders.
The biggest percentage gains were booked by small caps.
Software and electronic publishing group AND, which made its Amsterdam bourse debut last December at 3.30 guilders, added more than ten percent on the day and closed at 8.40 guilders.
"Since the big sellers are out of the stock and some retail investors want them at any price, the movement is quite big," said one dealer, but no fundamental reasons could be given.

Builder BAM benefitted from a broker upgrade saying the share traded at an 19 percent discount to its sector peers when looking at 1997 earnings. The share rose more than five percent to 114.80 guilders.
Computer software firm Baan, which is to report 1996 earnings later this afternoon, was also in demand, adding 3.40 guilders to close at 81.50 guilders.
Most analysts' forecasts are clustered around the consensus of $34 million, compared to last year's net profit of $15.3 million.

"They are driven by more than just a good feeling on the results -- Baan shares are also still benefiting from Salomon's upgrade a couple of days ago," said one dealer. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
